title: config: max_tokens is a flat 8192, six to sixteen times under what the model allows
description:
max_tokens goes to the wire verbatim (internal/provider/anthropicmsgs/request.go:52, openaichat/request.go:73) and nothing consults the registry's max_output, which rudy already fetches per model (provider/model.go:54). The default 8192 caps every request on models whose snapshot says 64000 or 128000, so a single large write or edit stops on max_tokens with a truncated tool input. Thinking hides half of it: buildParams raises max_tokens to budget+1024 when the thinking budget does not fit, so high thinking silently gets 17408 and every other level gets 8192.

Make the registry the source: empty or 0 means the model's max_output, an explicit value is clamped to it rather than sent and refused, and models list grows a column for the number rudy already knows. Config key work means a default, a catalogue entry, a contracts row and a regenerated example; validate() currently refuses max_tokens <= 0 and would have to accept 0 as 'the model's own'.

title: server: attaching to a parent does not replay a child's standing permission question
description:
subscribeLocked and deliverAttach (internal/server/session_live.go:415-464) loop over the attached session's own ls.standing when a client attaches mid-turn, and send one permission.requested per entry. They never look at a descendant's standing set.

So a client that reconnects to a parent while a subagent is awaiting permission sees nothing for that question. The child's call then waits out tool_timeout_ms, default 600000, with no prompt on screen. Live delivery works, since a child's question is routed up to the parent's askers when it is first raised; it is only the attach replay that misses it.

Reachable by the ordinary reconnect: close the TUI or drop the socket while a subagent is running an unsafe tool, then reattach.

Pre-existing relative to rudy-9nc rather than caused by it, and outside that issue's scope, which was the client holding one question instead of a set. Noted by the review of that fix, 2026-09-11.

Fix shape: the attach replay walks the same parent link the notification routing already walks, and sends a descendant's standing questions alongside the session's own. Depth is capped at one, so the walk does not recurse.
acceptance_criteria: A client attaching to a parent while a child's permission question stands receives that question and can answer it. Covered by a test that raises a child question, attaches a fresh client to the parent, and asserts the prompt arrives.
notes:
Widened 2026-09-11 by the whole-branch review: the gap is not only the standing question. A client reattaching to a parent mid-turn loses the child ENTIRELY. server.go:1181-1187 broadcasts a child's session_opened to watchers exactly once, at open, and subscribeLocked (session_live.go:436-465) replays only the attached session's own entries, turn state, in-flight tool states and standing questions. It never replays a live child's session_opened.

model.go is the only place RecordAgentCall is populated, and it populates it from that one broadcast. So a reattached client keeps receiving every child notification and drops all of them as another session's. The operator sees agent rows reading running with no child text ever appearing, and the child's prompt cannot be answered, so the call burns the full 600s tool_timeout_ms and returns an error.

The parent's own log names no live child, so this cannot be fixed by reading the log. It needs a replay path: the attachment walks the live children the way notification routing already walks the parent link. Note rudy-sgs covers an adjacent asker case.
close_reason: Fixed in 3d20277. The attach now walks down to every live child: its session_opened, which names the agent call its notifications render under, and its standing questions for an asker. Both halves of the issue, the widened session_opened gap and the standing permission question, are covered. Three tests, each verified by breaking the code: TestAttachToAParentNamesALiveChild and TestAttachToAParentHearsAChildsStandingQuestion drive a real session.resume and assert on what it delivered, with no hand-sent notification, and the second answers the child's question from the reattached connection and watches the tool run. TestAttachToParentReplaysOnlyAChildsSessionOpened holds the line that the rest of a child's log is still not replayed. Contracts amended first: the notifications section, the entry.appended and permission.requested rows and the session.resume row.

title: tui: with several prompts on screen nothing marks which one a keypress answers
description:
Since rudy-9nc the TUI holds every standing permission question rather than one, which is correct. But every prompt row renders the same 'allow once [y] allow for session [a] deny [n]' text, and nothing marks which row is focused() and will actually receive the keypress.

So an operator looking at two prompts for two different commands has no way to tell which one pressing y approves. That is misattribution on a consent surface: the operator believes they are approving the command they are looking at, and may be approving the other one. It is a milder relative of the coalescing defect fixed earlier in this wave, where an answer bound a call whose arguments the operator never saw.

Reachable whenever two unsafe tool calls are outstanding at once, which the concurrent dispatch in ADR 0028 makes ordinary and which the shipped examples/agents/reporter.md invites, since it lists bash, edit and write.

Deliberately not fixed alongside rudy-9nc: that issue was about tracking the questions, and this is about how focus is shown, which is a rendering and interaction design choice rather than a bug with one obvious fix. Options include marking the focused row, dimming the key hints on unfocused rows, or only rendering hints on the focused one.
acceptance_criteria: With more than one permission question on screen, it is unambiguous from the rendering which one a keypress will answer. Covered by a golden.
notes:
Raised to P1 on 2026-09-11 by the whole-branch review, which showed it is reachable from a single assistant message rather than needing two subagents. focused() (internal/tui/app/turn.go:217-222) picks the most recently ARRIVED prompt and its comment claims that is the one nearest the input. It is not. A parent's own prompt is appended at the end by Transcript.Prompt, while a child's is inserted mid-transcript by PromptFrom into insertAfterGroup, so a child's later prompt lands ABOVE the parent's and takes the keyboard.

Concretely: one assistant message emits agent(...) and bash('rm -rf build'). The parent's rm -rf prompt renders at the bottom, the child's bash prompt arrives and is inserted above it and takes the keyboard, and the operator reads the bottom row and presses y. That is consent bound to arguments the operator was not looking at, the same class as the coalescing defect closed at the asker earlier in this wave, left open at the keyboard.
close_reason: Fixed in fc93262. focused() is now row order rather than arrival order, so the keyboard answers the question nearest the input, and that row is the only one that draws the keys: every other question says where the keyboard is instead. Covered by the two_prompts golden and by TestTheKeyboardAnswersTheQuestionNearestTheInput, which drives the reachable case (one assistant message emitting agent() and bash(rm -rf build)) and fails against both the old focus rule and unmarked rows.

title: tui: a second permission prompt overwrites the first, so one call hangs unanswerable
description:
m.turn.prompt and m.turn.asked in internal/tui/app are single slots holding one outstanding permission question. That was sufficient while the turn runner invoked tools one at a time, because only one question could stand per session.

ADR 0028 made the tool calls of one assistant message run concurrently (runner.go dispatches them together), so several can be awaiting permission at once. The server already models this correctly: it keeps a map of standing questions per session and sends the whole sorted set to a client attaching mid-turn. The TUI does not. The second question overwrites the first on the keyboard while the first's row is still on screen, so the operator answers the second and the first can never be answered. That call then waits on its context and fails at tool_timeout_ms, which defaults to 600000.

Same symptom as rudy-ssz one level in: a permission question that exists, is displayed or was displayed, and cannot be resolved.

Introduced by this wave rather than pre-existing, and reachable whenever a model emits two unsafe tool calls in one message, or delegates to two subagents that each touch an unsafe tool.

Fix shape: the TUI holds a queue or map keyed by session id and tool_use id, matching the server's standing set, and the composer answers the focused one. The on-attach path already receives the full standing set, so the client has the data it needs.
acceptance_criteria: Two permission questions outstanding at once are both answerable, in any order, and neither row is left unresolvable. Covered by a test that raises two concurrent questions and answers them both.
close_reason: Fixed in 0cccf15. turnControl.prompt/asked (single *protocol.PermissionRequested) replaced with maps keyed by promptKey{sessionID, toolUseID}, matching the server's own standing set, plus an arrival-order slice; focused() returns the most recently arrived standing question, the one the composer answers. session.answer now carries its key in CallResultMsg.Name (m.answer uses callNamed), so callResult/callFailed resolve or reask exactly the one question a given response is for, not the whole set. Covered by TestTwoConcurrentQuestionsBothResolve (internal/tui/app/turn_test.go): raises two questions on one session, answers the second (most recent) first, then the first, asserts both session.answer calls land with the right tool_use ids and no question is left standing. Verified by deliberate breakage: temporarily made addPrompt wipe the previous entry (the old single-slot bug, reproduced exactly) and watched the test fail at 'focused after t2 = <nil>, want t1' before restoring. Also fixed the coupled MINOR: server.go's session_opened broadcast (rudy-ssz's fix) now guards len(ls.entries) > 0 before indexing ls.entries[0]. go test -race on internal/tui/... and internal/server/... (both transports) and make check all green; no golden moved.

title: tui: a subagent's permission prompt is dropped, so an unsafe tool in a child hangs until the tool timeout
description:
A child session has no asker of its own, so askers() (internal/server/session_live.go) walks up and sends its permission.requested to the PARENT's askers. The parent's TUI receives it carrying the CHILD's session_id, and model.go's session-scope gate drops any notification whose session id is not the one on screen. Nobody ever sees the prompt and nobody can answer it.

The child's tool call then waits on its context. tool_timeout_ms defaults to 600000, so the call hangs for ten minutes and fails, with no indication to the operator of what it was waiting for.

Pre-existing since the plugins wave, but the subagents wave makes it reachable in the ordinary case: the shipped examples/agents/reporter.md lists bash, edit and write, all of which are tool.Unsafe, so the default example subagent hits this the first time it runs a command.

Two parts to a fix. The TUI has to render a child's permission.requested under the agent row that owns that child, which the routing work in task 6 and the rendering work in task 7 already make possible. And m.answer() hardcodes the parent's session id, so it must send the session the prompt actually came from. Answering is deliberately NOT subscription gated (handleAnswer checks cn.asker only, and the contracts record that a child borrowing its parent's asker is the mechanism working), so the parent's TUI is entitled to answer for the child.
acceptance_criteria: A subagent that calls an unsafe tool raises a prompt the operator sees, rendered under the agent call that opened it, and answering it allows or denies that child's call. Covered by a test that drives a child's permission request to the parent's TUI and answers it.
close_reason: Fixed in b44aebc (tui) and e05c156 (server, the bootstrap gap that made the whole path unreachable on the real agent-tool path). Render: Transcript.PromptFrom/AnsweredFrom (transcript.go), tool()'s prompt-suppression key made origin-aware, Row.ToolState + SetToolState for the awaiting_permission gap (render.go, row.go). Answer: turn.go's answer()/reask() now target the session the prompt actually named (p.SessionID) instead of m.session.SessionID, via clearPrompt/takeDownPrompt/answeredFrom. Covered by TestAChildsPermissionPromptRendersAndAnswers and TestADecisionFromElsewhereTakesDownAChildsPrompt (internal/tui/app/subagent_test.go), plus TestAChildsPromptSuppressesItsOwnToolRowAndIndents and TestAChildsToolStateShowsAwaitingPermission (internal/tui/transcript/transcript_test.go). Every assertion verified by deliberate breakage: reverted p.SessionID to m.session.SessionID (test failed naming the parent instead of the child), removed the childNotification PermissionDecision cleanup (test failed, standing question survived), reverted the tool() suppression key to bare (test failed, tool row drew alongside the prompt), reverted PromptFrom's stamp (test failed, origin unset), no-op'd SetToolState (test failed, stayed on running). make check green (fmt-check, vendor-types, vet, lint 0 issues, full race suite both transports).

title: server: a child's tool view is not bounded by its parent's, so delegation escapes a restricted tool list
description:
applyAgent (server.go:1193) builds a child session's tool view with plugin.NewToolView(s.d.Plugins, def.Tools, deny). That starts from the whole plugin registry and applies only the child definition's own list plus the agent deny. It never intersects with the parent session's tool view.

So a parent whose definition is [read, agent] cannot write, but can call agent with a definition whose tools key is absent (meaning every tool) and the child gets bash, edit and write. Removing a tool from an agent's list is the only way to restrict it, so delegation being able to hand out what the parent does not hold makes the restriction meaningless.

Exists today, independent of the subagents wave. ADR 0028 decision 5 makes the intersection part of that wave: a caller may only narrow a tool list, never widen it.
acceptance_criteria: A child session's tool view is the intersection of its own definition's list and its parent's effective list. A parent restricted to [read, agent] cannot open a child that holds bash, edit or write, whatever the child's definition says. Covered by a server test that opens a child under a permissive definition from a restricted parent and asserts the child's offered tools.
notes:
Reopened 2026-09-10. The first fix (41bb2b8) closed the live-open path only. A child session is always cold by the time anyone resumes it, because the subagents plugin closes the child's connection on every call (plugins/subagents/plugin.go:94). applyAgentFromLog (server.go:1242) never sets ls.parent, so parentToolNames returns nil and a resumed or forked child is rebuilt with its definition's full list. Parent [read, agent], child opened under a permissive definition, resume the child: it holds bash, edit and write. That is this issue verbatim, one resume later, and TestResumedChildKeepsItsOwnList asserted that set as the expected outcome.

Not model-reachable today since the model cannot call resume or fork, but a client or plugin can, and the real plugin puts the child's session id in the tool result text the model reads.

Fix direction: the session's resolved tool set is persisted on its session_opened entry at open time and replayed on resume, so the invariant holds without depending on whether the parent is still live.
close_reason: session_opened now records the resolved tool set at open time and applyAgentFromLog replays it on resume and fork instead of recomputing from the definition; TestChildSessionThroughThePluginClass proves it on the real subagents plugin path (live open, resume, fork), and TestResumedChildKeepsItsOwnList/TestForkedChildKeepsItsOwnList cover it directly. go test -race on both transports and make check are green.

title: memory: Remember read-modify-writes a concept with no lock, so concurrent calls lose a revision
description:
memory-go's Remember (write.go:36) reads the existing concept (line 52), builds a revision from that base via Revise or Create, then writes it back. No lock, no O_EXCL, no flock. Two concurrent calls on the same title both read the same base and the later write silently discards the earlier revision.

Latent today only because rudy's turn runner invokes tools one at a time. ADR 0028 decision 2 makes every tool call concurrent, which makes this live.

ADR 0028 decision 3 puts the obligation on the tool that owns the state: the rudy memory plugin serializes its own invocations so rudy is correct regardless. That is the fix that lands in this repo. This issue tracks the real fix in memory-go, which any other memory-go caller still needs.
acceptance_criteria: memory-go's Remember is safe under concurrent calls on one title: no revision is lost. Covered by a test that runs concurrent Remember calls on the same title under -race.

title: subagents wave: concurrent tool dispatch, live child visibility, agents from plugins
description:
ADR 0025 names subagents as the next feature. Three audits (2026-09-10) established the shape.

Spine: a running tool call becomes addressable. runner.go holds one cancel slot (869), one single-consumer interrupt flag (878) and one RunningTool state (854); Observer.StateChanged carries no tool identity. Replacing those with a per-tool_use_id keyed set is what both halves of the wave need: N concurrent calls need per-call cancel and broadcast interrupt, and the TUI needs per-call identity to render a live subagent.

Policy: safe tools dispatch concurrently, unsafe tools stay serial, using the existing tool.Safe/tool.Unsafe split. agent is Safe so subagents fan out; bash and edit are Unsafe so the git-index and same-file hazards cannot arise; the session-scope double-ask (Gate.Evaluate reads allowances at entry, the allow appends at runner.go:518) cannot arise either since the asking tools stay serial.

Visibility: the child's broadcastObsLocked (session_live.go:316) also delivers to the parent's non-plugin subscribers, tagged with the child session id already in every payload. Mirrors the existing upward askers() walk (session_live.go:201). Not session.watch: ownSession (server.go:428) gates submit and interrupt on subscription, so a watch would grant the TUI write rights over the child.

Agents from plugins: Host.RegisterAgent following RegisterProvider's shape; resolveAgent (server.go:1177) merges Registry.AgentDefs() into its hardcoded two-root literal. Precedence is disk over plugins: user config, then workspace .rudy/agents, then plugin-contributed.

Folded in: the agent tool description is already stale (built once in Init from the config dir, so workspace defs are already missing), and rudy-ulb is a race in the cancel path this rewrites.
acceptance_criteria: ADR 0028 written and accepted. rudy-contracts.md rows edited before code. Concurrent dispatch under safe/unsafe policy with per-call cancel and interrupt. Parent TUI renders a running subagent live. A plugin can contribute an agent definition, linked and spawned. rudy-ulb closed. make check green.
close_reason: delivered: concurrent tool dispatch with per-call cancel and interrupt, a child's notifications reaching its parent's subscribers, a plugin able to contribute an agent definition, and the agent tool roster moved from a stale build-once description to a session_opened hook (ADR 0028, tasks 1-10)

title: kernel: nothing writes rudy.log, so an intermittent failure leaves no trail
description: docs/specs/rudy-contracts.md promises $XDG_CACHE_HOME/rudy/rudy.log (slog JSON lines) and the config keys log.level and log.file. grep slog. finds nothing outside the vendor SDKs: there is no logger, no file and no keys. An intermittent non-zero exit or a client that quits on its own has no evidence to read afterwards, which is what this cost tonight. Wire a slog JSON handler to log.file at log.level, defaulting to the contracted path, and add the two keys to the catalogue, the defaults, the example and the contracts rows so the drift guards go green with the UNSHIPPED markers removed.
close_reason: rudy.log is written by every command that boots the kernel: JSON slog lines at log.level on log.file, pid on every record, notices mirrored at warn, and records for start, plugin state, session open resume and detach, turn start completed and failed, connection open and close, the socket bind and the exit path. Commits 584a0d5, 45ac846, a477a01. Covered end to end by a print run read back from the file, verified to fail without the emitters.

title: server: a resume racing the last detach gets unavailable instead of the session
description: TestDetachRacesResume fails about one run in twenty under -race: session.resume loses the race with the last subscriber's session.close and comes back jsonrpc -32006 'session unavailable, retry' rather than attached to a live session. Pre-existing at 844d6ea, reproduced in a clean worktree, so it is not the mid-turn command or the registry collapse. Either the server has to hold the resume until the close settles and re-open, or the contract says a racing resume may be told to retry and the test has to say so too. Decide which, then make the test deterministic rather than a one-in-twenty.

title: plugin: a plugin cannot bundle the MCP server it needs
description:
A plugin that wants somebody else's hosted tools has no way to bring them: mcp.toml is the operator's file, written by rudy mcp add, and a plugin cannot declare a server it depends on. The case that raised it is keyless web search, which is what pi's web extension does out of the box by speaking MCP to Exa's hosted server (mcp.exa.ai/mcp); rudy ships an MCP client with an http transport already, so the missing piece is declaration and lifecycle rather than protocol.

Questions the design has to answer, none of them decided: who owns the entry, since a plugin must not rewrite the operator's mcp.toml; when the server starts and stops relative to the plugin that declared it; what the operator's override and off switch look like; how tool names from a bundled server avoid colliding with another server's; and the trust question that gates the rest, which is that a declared stdio server is a plugin choosing a command rudy then runs. ADR 0025 makes an installed plugin's code the operator's decision already, but a bundled stdio server widens that to whatever the manifest names, so the answer may be http transports only, or explicit consent per server at install.
acceptance_criteria: A plugin declares the MCP servers it needs, the operator sees and can refuse or override each one, the servers start and stop with the plugin, and ADR records the trust decision for stdio versus http.

Terminal durability failures are already safe: turn.ErrTerminalDurability's text is fixed and the cause only reaches the Server log (ADR 0037, task rudy-4tf.1.11). This is the rest of the surface. title: sandbox: run tool calls in a remote Firecracker microVM
description:
Run the model's tool calls, and possibly whole subagent sessions, inside a Firecracker microVM on a remote host rather than on the operator's machine. The workspace is mounted or synced in, the tool runs against it in the VM, and results come back over the protocol. Nothing the model runs can touch the host.

Why now. Two things this codebase already does make the case sharper than it was. ADR 0025's install wave adds a manifest build command that runs arbitrary code from a source the operator named, and the honest answer to 'where is it safe to run that' is a throwaway VM. ADR 0028 made tool calls of one message run concurrently and lets a session fan out to several subagents, so a per-call or per-subagent VM is a natural unit: each gets a clean machine, they cannot contend for one working tree, and a subagent that goes wrong is discarded with its VM.

Open questions, deliberately not decided here: which tools go remote (bash and write obviously, read and grep perhaps not); how the workspace gets in and changes get back out (mount, rsync, git); whether the VM is per call, per turn, per session or per subagent; where the VMs run and how rudy reaches them; and whether this is a plugin providing the tools or a mode the kernel applies to every tool. Firecracker itself needs a Linux host with KVM, so the remote half is not optional on a Mac.

Filed 2026-09-11 at Guy's request during the subagents wave handoff.

title: server: a plain client is not subscription gated on interrupt, set_*, compact, close or shell
description:
ownSession (internal/server/server.go:429) only runs when cn.plugin != "", so the subscription check applies to plugin connections and to nothing else. handleInterrupt (server.go:556) does not even take a *conn: it resolves the session id and calls the runner. The same is true for set_mode, set_model, set_thinking, set_title, session.compact, session.close and session.shell.

So any connected client may drive any live session on the machine by id, whether or not it ever attached to it. session.shell is the sharpest of these, since it runs a command ungated by the Gate on the grounds that the operator typed it themselves (ADR 0023).

Pre-existing and not introduced by the subagents wave, and it applies to every session rather than to children specifically. The wave did close the two paths it put within reach: session.submit and session.interrupt now refuse a child session from an unsubscribed connection, because routing a child's notifications to its parent's client is what first made a running child's id reachable.

Note that a guard here is a rail rather than a boundary while session.resume authz remains "any session on this machine": an unsubscribed client can resume a session and then act on it legitimately. Closing this properly means deciding what subscription is for, which is a design question rather than a patch.
acceptance_criteria: Either every session method that mutates a session is subscription gated for every caller class, or the contracts record which are deliberately not and why, with session.resume's authz reconciled against whichever is chosen.
close_reason: Recorded rather than gated: contracts caller-class section and the README's trust model now say attachment is not a permission and why, which is the second half of this issue's own acceptance criteria. A gate would need session.resume's any-session-on-this-machine authz reconciled first; file that separately if the trust boundary ever moves off the socket.

title: gate: the dangerous set only ever matches bash, though config documents a bare tool name
description:
Gate.Dangerous (internal/gate/matcher.go:32-34) returns false for every tool except bash, so only a bash prefix can ever be dangerous. The config surface says otherwise: docs/specs/rudy-contracts.md lists permissions.dangerous with the proposed shape 'tool' or 'tool:prefix', and the contents are on the open list. An operator reading that would reasonably write a bare tool name and get silence, not an error and not an effect.

Found during the subagents wave Task 1 review (2026-09-10). It is why 'empty matcher prefix' currently implies 'not dangerous', a coupling nothing states and nothing enforces. ADR 0028 decision 4 deliberately does not rely on it: settlement reads an explicit Dangerous bit from the Gate rather than inferring one from the matcher shape, so this bug does not affect that path. Fixing it here is what keeps that independence honest.

Either make a bare tool name work, or refuse it at config load with a message saying only bash prefixes are supported, and correct the contracts row either way.
acceptance_criteria: A bare tool name in permissions.dangerous either marks that tool dangerous for every input, or is refused at config load with a clear message. The contracts row and internal/config/docs.go agree with whichever is chosen. Covered by a gate test for a non-bash dangerous entry.
close_reason: Wrappers are expanded and matched three deep, and an entry may name a tool (tool: or tool:prefix) as well as a bash prefix. Contracts row, config comment and gate tests updated; 14 wrapper shapes covered.

title: tui: any inline frame that shrinks strands its rows on screen (the picker, the slash menu)
description: In inline mode a picker grows the live frame; the terminal scrolls, and closing the picker repaints below the rows it left, so the picker's rows stay in scrollback as ghosts. Reproduced under tmux in TUI Task 10's real path. Same mechanism ADR 0013 decision 4 uses to commit rows. Fix candidates: a constant-height inline frame (the picker replaces the editor slot at the editor's height and scrolls inside it), or a Bubble Tea change. Altscreen is unaffected.
notes:
Reproduced 2026-09-09 under a pty with ui.render=inline, rudy at cb6da2a. Opening the slash menu on a fresh session grows the live frame by 9 rows; typing the draft past a command name closes it, and 8 of the 9 rows stay ON SCREEN above the new frame, not just in scrollback. The 9th is overwritten because the shrunk frame is redrawn at the bottom of where the tall one sat.

Mechanism, from charm.land/bubbletea/v2@v2.0.9 cursed_renderer.go flush(): an inline view sizes the renderer's cell buffer to the frame's own height (frameArea.Max.Y = content.Height()), erases and repaints only that area, and drops buffer lines from the top when the frame is taller than the terminal. Nothing owns the rows a taller frame occupied once it shrinks, so nothing erases them. Not specific to the picker: every inline frame height change has it, and the editor growing and shrinking with a multi-line draft strands a row too (invisible only because the stranded row is the near-empty prompt row).

So the fix has to bound the inline frame's height rather than any one component's: a constant-height live region, where the picker, the menu and the editor scroll inside their slot instead of adding rows. v2.0.9 is the newest v2, so there is no upstream bump to wait for.

Not what a default install meets any more: ADR 0015 made altscreen the default, and altscreen is unaffected.

title: memory: the finalize fold's note never lands; the session log is closed before the background fold ends

The memory plugin folds on session_closed with finalize=true. fireSessionClosed fires the hook and returns as soon as handlers return; the memory plugin starts the fold on its own goroutine (startFold) and returns immediately, then closeClaimed calls ls.sess.Close() and the server deletes the session from s.live. Observed: session 01M22RD2T9HE8HKBQAM75Q6Z7H folded at 2026-09-09T09:37:51Z, wrote one observation and the summary
projects/github.com/guygrigsby/rudy/session-summaries/20260909T093628Z-rudy-cline-pass-kimi-k3.md, and its entries.jsonl has no note entry of any kind. Every rudy -p session today is the same: the summaries land, no note ever does.

Decide who keeps a session open for a plugin's background work: either the server holds the session until in-flight plugin jobs drain (a contract change: session_closed handlers currently only get hook_timeout_ms), or the memory plugin stops promising a note for the finalize fold and says so in the contracts.

title: beads pre-commit hook writes a stray issues.jsonl in linked worktrees
description:
In a linked git worktree the bd pre-commit hook resolves the beads dir to the worktree root instead of .beads/, so every commit creates and stages a root issues.jsonl (221 lines) that lands in the commit, then rewrites .beads/issues.jsonl and deletes the root copy, leaving the worktree dirty. Reproduced on bd 1.0.2 (Homebrew) in /private/tmp/rudy-acp-task11: a commit of one unrelated file carried issues.jsonl with it.

Violates the ACP plan's rule that parallel worker worktrees never mutate or export beads state.

Mitigated locally: extensions.worktreeConfig is enabled on this repo and each worker worktree sets core.hooksPath to .git/no-beads-hooks (an empty dir), so beads hooks run only in the main worktree. Drop the override when bd fixes the discovery, and report it upstream (gastownhall/beads).

A nested module falls outside ./..., so go vet ./... and golangci-lint run ./... in make check no longer see it. gofmt -l . still does, and internal/server's TestMain still compiles it, so a type error fails tests; but a vet or lint finding in the example is now invisible to CI. title: pluginstore: a lock touched by an older binary loses kind, turning a go or https entry into path
description: The lock's kind, ref and digest keys are new. A binary from before them reads such a lock fine (go-toml is non-strict) but its Write drops the three keys, so one rudy plugins disable on the old binary rewrites a go: or https: entry without kind. The new binary then derives kind=path from the empty commit and the next update runs stagePath on a module path and fails at git clone. Documented in the contracts kind row. Fix shape: derive kind from the source prefix when the key is absent, which is unambiguous for go: and for .tar.gz, and only fall back to commit-presence for the rest. Surfaced by the whole-branch review, 2026-09-11.

title: pluginstore: the stale sweep removes a .old backup after an hour, losing the only copy after an unattended mid swap failure
description: sweepStaleStages removes *.old after staleStageAge, one hour. If a three-step swap fails between renaming dir to dir.old and renaming the stage in, and nobody runs update again within the hour, the sweep deletes the only copy. Install then refuses as already installed because the lock still names it. Narrow: needs a filesystem error mid swap and an hour of neglect. Fix shape: a .old whose sibling dir is absent is a backup, not a stale stage; restore it rather than sweep it. Surfaced by the whole-branch review of the plugin install wave, 2026-09-11.

title: pluginstore: the store-owned GOMODCACHE is left read-only, so rm -rf of the data root fails
description: go mod download writes the module cache read-only by design. rudy creates Root/plugins/.gomodcache for go: installs and nothing in rudy ever removes or chmods it, so rm -rf ~/.local/share/rudy fails with Permission denied. Verified by the whole-branch review of the plugin install wave, 2026-09-11. Fix shape: uninstall of the last go: plugin, or a rudy plugins clean, runs go clean -modcache against that GOMODCACHE, or the store chmods the tree writable on removal.

title: pluginstore: an https tarball's entry count is unbounded since the stream cap moved to bytes written
description:
The task 5 fix for sparse entries replaced cappedReader over the gzip stream with a budget on bytes written per entry. That correctly bounds disk usage, but zero-byte entries and directories consume no write budget and have no count limit, so the number of entries is now bounded only by the download cap. Measured by the re-review: one million unique directory entries gzip to 4.7 MiB, so a download well inside maxDownloadBytes carries roughly 54 million MkdirAll and OpenFile calls and inodes. The old cappedReader stopped at about 512K entries.

Severity is limited: an https install runs the manifest's build command anyway, so the archive is already semi-trusted. But it is a bound this diff removed. Fix is a few lines: keep a cap on decompressed stream bytes alongside the write budget, or add an entry-count cap. Surfaced 2026-09-11 by the task 5 re-review of the plugin install wave.
close_reason: Entry count capped at maxTarEntries (20000) in scanTarball, refused before the first write, with a test that a 20001-entry archive well inside the download cap is rejected and leaves the stage empty.

title: pluginstore: the update swap is remove then rename, so a filesystem error mid swap loses the checkout
description:
Update swaps its built stage into plugins/<name> with os.RemoveAll(dir) followed by os.Rename(stage, dir), because Rename cannot replace a non-empty directory. If RemoveAll fails partway, or succeeds and the Rename then fails, the function returns before keep is set and the deferred cleanup removes the stage as well: the plugin has no checkout on disk at all while the lock still names it as installed. Both windows need a filesystem-level error, not an ordinary failed build, so they are narrow; but the doc comment claims any failure leaves the live checkout untouched, and here it does not.

Install does not have this problem because its dest is checked absent before the Rename, which is then a true atomic create.

Fix shape: a three-step swap. Rename dir to dir.old, rename stage to dir, RemoveAll dir.old. The worst remaining failure orphans a backup instead of destroying the plugin.

Surfaced by the task 1 re-review of the plugin install wave, 2026-09-11. Task 3 of that plan restructures Update for ref pinning and is the natural place to land this.
close_reason: fixed: swapCheckout renames dir aside before renaming stage in, so a failed swap orphans dir.old instead of destroying the checkout

title: cli: rudy plugin install and update run with no signal context, so a hung build cannot be cancelled in process
description:
cmd/rudy/main.go calls ExecuteContext(context.Background()) with no signal.NotifyContext. serve.go and print.go install their own, but the plugin verbs do not, so the ctx threaded into pluginstore.Install and Update, and from there into git and the manifest's build subprocess via exec.CommandContext, is never cancelled. A build that hangs under rudy plugin install can only be stopped by the terminal's SIGINT reaching the process group, not by any in-process path.

Pre-existing: the same ctx already reached the git calls before the build step landed. Surfaced by the task 1 review of the plugin install wave, 2026-09-11. Fix shape: wrap the root context in signal.NotifyContext for SIGINT and SIGTERM the way serve does, so Ctrl-C cancels the subprocess cleanly and the stage is removed.

title: server: attach hands a parent's asker a child's question even when the child has its own asker
description:
watchAttachment delivers to a parent's attaching asker any question standing on a live child, unconditionally. Live routing does not do that: askers() walks up to the parent only when the child has no askers of its own (len(out) == 0).

So if a human has resumed the child directly, giving it an asker, and then attaches to the parent, the parent's asker is shown a question the child's own asker is already handling. Both can answer; the first wins and the second gets a conflict.

Reachable only by resuming a child session directly, which the CLI deliberately skips when picking a session to continue. It costs an extra prompt, and the arguments shown are the real ones, so it is not a consent hole, only a divergence between the attach path and the live path.

Found by the scoped re-review of the subagents wave's final fix, 2026-09-11. Fix shape: apply the same has-its-own-askers test the live walk uses.
acceptance_criteria: A parent attaching while a child has its own asker is not shown that child's standing question. The attach path and askers() use one predicate.

title: plugin: agent definition validation is duplicated between the linked and spawned paths
description:
host.RegisterAgent (internal/plugin/registry.go:600-606) and Spawned.RegisterAgent (internal/plugin/spawned.go:658-666) each independently check that a description is non-empty and that thinking is one of off, low, medium or high. Two hand-kept copies of the same rule.

Harmless today. A linked plugin's Init failure surfaces only as error text in a status and a notice (registry.go:112-115) and never goes through protocol.ErrorFrom, so the missing ErrInvalidArgument wrap on the linked path cannot reach a wire response. But TestRegisterAgentValidates (registry_test.go:606) asserts only that the error is non-nil, not its code, so widening or narrowing one check without the other diverges silently with nothing to catch it.

Raised by the task 9 review of the subagents wave, 2026-09-11, which verified the gap is real by reverting the spawned check and watching an internal error code surface where invalid_argument was required.

Fix shape: one validator over agentdef.Definition, called by both paths, returning an error the spawned path wraps for the wire. agentdef.parse enforces the same rules for a definition read from a file and is the natural third caller.
acceptance_criteria: One validator enforces an agent definition's rules for the file, linked and spawned paths. A test asserts the error code the wire returns, not merely that an error occurred.

title: turn: a failing tool call does not cancel its siblings, so a doomed turn waits for them
description:
Since the subagents wave made tool calls of one assistant message run concurrently (ADR 0028), a call that fails the turn no longer stops the calls running beside it. The turn waits for every sibling to finish before it ends.

Not a correctness bug: each sibling's result is appended and the turn ends on the first outcome in call order, so the outcome is deterministic. It is an unspecified behaviour change in latency. A turn that is already doomed can sit waiting on a long subagent or a slow shell command that nobody will read the result of.

Raised by the Task 3 review, 2026-09-10, and deliberately deferred rather than fixed there: cancelling siblings on failure is a policy decision about whether a sibling's partial work is worth keeping, and it deserves its own pass rather than being decided inside a scheduler change.
acceptance_criteria: Either a failing call cancels its siblings and the behaviour is recorded in the contracts, or the current waiting behaviour is recorded as intended with the reason. Whichever is chosen is covered by a test.

description: The TUI switches to a /fork result by session.close then session.resume, because the server already attached the connection in forkAt and subscribeLocked has no dedupe. The close drops the fork to zero connections, closeIfUnusedLocked closes it (session_closed hooks, the memory finalize fold), and the resume cold-loads it and fires session_opened{Resumed:true}. Give the client a way to adopt an already attached session without the round trip: either command.run answers the fork's SessionInfo, or session.resume on a session this connection already holds is a no-op that answers the info. Found in TUI Task 8 review.

title: server: a /fork notice renders twice, sent as both a notification and the command.run result

Found in TUI Task 8. Decide which one carries it (the contract row for command.run says the result) and drop the other.
notes: The TUI stops drawing the result's notice (9517745) as a mitigation; the server still sends both. Root cause: handleCommandRun's four branches call cn.notify(NotifyNotice) and return CommandRunResult{Notice}. Drop the notify; the result carries it per the contract.

title: provider: Message has per-role fields that are meaningless for other roles, and wants to be a sum type
description:
provider.Message carries Content for most roles and Results for RoleToolResult, and each is meaningless for the other. It already had that shape with ToolUseID and IsError before the subagents wave; the wave replaced those with Results and so kept the carve-out rather than introducing it.

Noted by the Task 3 implementer, 2026-09-10, as an honest observation about where the type is heading: it is one more role away from genuinely wanting to be a sum type, and until then every reader has to know which fields are live for which role.

Not urgent and not a bug. Recorded so the next person adding a role makes the choice deliberately instead of adding a third carve-out.
acceptance_criteria: Either provider.Message becomes a sum type over its roles, or the per-role field validity is documented on the type so a reader does not have to infer it from the codecs.
